claims.claim: On the tRPC benchmark, codeblast's predicted affected-test set contained every test file that actually failed, for all 28 mutants the test suite killed.
claims.metric: mutation-testing recall: fraction of killed mutants whose real failing-test file set is a subset of the predicted affected-test file set
claims.method: 30 mutants injected one at a time into test-covered TypeScript functions (throw on the function's first line); the full vitest suite is run per mutant to obtain the ground-truth failing-test files; the file is then restored. 2 of the 30 mutants were not killed by the suite (dead code path or type-only) and are excluded from the ratio.

claims.claim: The weekly acceptance workflow fails the build if the tRPC graph drops below 900 files or 15000 edges, or the graphql-tools graph below 300 files or 8000 edges.
claims.value: tRPC > 900 files and > 15000 edges; graphql-tools > 300 files and > 8000 edges
claims.metric: hard assertions on files and edges row counts in the generated SQLite graph, used as sentinels against silent file loss
claims.method: The acceptance workflow indexes each benchmark repo, asserts the row counts, then runs mutation testing behind a 100% recall gate; a scheduled failure opens an issue labelled acceptance-regression.

claims.claim: Indexing the tRPC monorepo produces a 6248-node, 17072-edge graph across 957 files with zero failures.
claims.value: 957 files, 6248 nodes, 17072 edges, 14725 blind spots, 0 failures
claims.metric: row counts reported by `codeblast index` for the generated SQLite graph; blind_spots counts unresolved and dynamic references, which is expected to be large on a real TypeScript monorepo and is not an error count
claims.method: Single `codeblast index` run of published codeblast 0.3.0 against a shallow clone of trpc/trpc at commit 66d0544. Deterministic given the same commit and version; counts drift with upstream commits, so the commit is part of the claim. Wall-clock seconds are machine-dependent and deliberately not claimed.
claims.repro: git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/trpc/trpc.git && git -C trpc checkout 66d0544 && npx codeblast@0.3.0 index ./trpc --db /tmp/graph.db

claims.claim: Every page under docs/ carries a description, a canonical URL, an Open Graph block and JSON-LD, and no two pages share a title — `codeblast archmap` emits them, and this is what keeps the generated maps findable.
claims.value: one head block per page, titles distinct
claims.metric: the four head elements on every docs/*.html, plus the set of titles
claims.method: src/archmap-html.ts builds the block from --repo-url / --site-url / --og-image (all optional: absent flags mean no canonical and no og:url rather than a guessed one) and names each page by repository and kind, so an architecture map, a blast-radius overlay and a change map of the same repo do not collide. The check scans every committed page.

claims.claim: Every page in this repository that animates also handles `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, so the page must stay readable and complete when it is off.
claims.value: no animated page without a reduced-motion branch
claims.method: the check walks every committed .html page, and where it finds an animation it requires a reduced-motion branch. It does not judge what the fallback does — only that one exists, because a missing branch is invisible in review and obvious to the person who gets motion sickness.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

pages = [p for p in list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html')) + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html'))
         if p.name != 'template.html']
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if re.search(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes', t):
        animated += 1
        if 'prefers-reduced-motion' not in t:
            missing.append(p.name)
print('pages', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert not missing
PY
